title: Gum paste peony
subtitle: a layered sugar flower built petal by petal on a wire stem
excerpt: A gum paste peony is a sugar flower built from individually shaped petals wired onto a central ball and dried in a curved foam former between stages. Each layer of petals goes on before the previous layer has fully dried so they hold a cupped shape. A finished peony hardens overnight and keeps indefinitely at room temperature away from moisture.
sourceNotes: Gum paste flower technique developed in sugarcraft from the mid-twentieth century onward, building on earlier sugar flower traditions. Wired petal construction standard in competition and wedding-cake sugarcraft manuals.

glossaryTerms.definition: A sugar paste made with tylose or gum tragacanth that dries hard and can be rolled very thin. Used for modelled decorations and sugar flowers where a firm, dry finish is needed.

content.text: A gum paste peony is a sugar flower made from

rolled thin, cut into petal shapes, thinned further at the edges, and wired in layers around a central ball. You build it over two sessions, with each layer of inner petals drying upright before the outer petals go on. The finished flower hardens completely overnight.

You will need petal cutters in two sizes: one for inner petals, one for outer. You also need a foam pad, a ball-end modelling tool, florists' wire (24 gauge), and florists' tape. An egg carton or apple tray works as a curved former to hold the petals in shape while they dry.

Roll a ball of gum paste the size of a large grape. Push a hooked 24-gauge wire through the base of the ball and pull the hook down into the paste to anchor it. Leave upright in a foam block overnight to dry completely.
Once dry, tape over the hook with florists' tape, pulling the tape tightly so it bonds as it stretches.
Roll gum paste to about 2 mm thick on a lightly greased board. Cut 5 petals with the smaller cutter. Work with one petal at a time and keep the rest under cling film; gum paste dries out quickly.
Place a petal on the foam pad. Roll the ball tool around the outer edge in a back-and-forth motion to thin and frill the edge. The centre of the petal stays thicker.

Brush a little edible glue onto the lower third of the petal. Wrap it around the dry centre ball so the tip of the petal stands above the ball. Press the base firmly to the wire below the ball to secure it.

Add the remaining 4 inner petals evenly around the centre, overlapping each one slightly. Pinch the base of each petal lightly to create a cupped shape. Leave upright for at least 2 hours until firm before adding the outer petals.
Cut 7 petals with the larger cutter. Thin and frill each one on the foam pad as before.
Brush edible glue at the base of each outer petal and press it against the wire below the inner petals, angling it slightly outward. Space the 7 petals evenly around the flower.
Rest the flower face-down in a shallow curved former; an egg carton cup works well. The wire should point up through the base. This holds the outer petals in a slightly open position as they dry.
Leave to dry overnight. The petals will harden in the curved position and hold their shape permanently.

attrs.problem: Petals cracking when the edges are being thinned
attrs.avoid: Avoid rolling gum paste too thin before cutting; it becomes brittle.
attrs.fix: Knead a tiny amount of vegetable shortening into the gum paste to soften it. Work quickly once rolled out.

attrs.problem: Petals drooping and not holding a cupped shape
attrs.avoid: Avoid placing the inner petals while they are still very soft; they will collapse rather than hold.
attrs.fix: Let each inner petal rest on the foam for 5 minutes before attaching it, so it has stiffened slightly but is still pliable enough to press onto the centre.

attrs.problem: Outer petals falling away from the flower
attrs.avoid: Avoid using too little edible glue; a dry petal will not bond to the wire or the petals beneath it.
attrs.fix: Apply edible glue to the lower third of the petal and hold it in place for 30 seconds while it begins to bond. The glue sets fully as the paste dries.
